_description: A 'suicide burn': free-fall (no thrust) for the first 3.74s, then 7 discrete Up-arrow presses fired 20ms apart (each one +2250 thrust via increaseThrust(), reaching 15750 total) to decelerate sharply before touchdown. Timeline found by src/verify/design-soft-landing.mjs (idealized fixed-40ms-tick simulation of the reference physics.js, predicting ~0.58 m/s). An earlier 9-press/5.0s candidate (idealized prediction ~0.97 m/s) measured 2.05-2.06 m/s against the REAL rebuild in a browser - over the 2 m/s threshold - because real Playwright/CDP dispatch latency between 9 rapid keydown calls delays full thrust more than the idealized simulation accounts for (a systematic effect, not the random per-tick jitter an earlier +/-40%-jitter check had tested for). This 7-press/3.74s config was chosen by testing several candidates directly against the real rebuild and was then repeated 3x for consistency: measured 1.01, 0.96, 1.08 m/s across those 3 real runs, all comfortably softLanded - see docs/KIRO_NOTES.md for the full account of finding and fixing the first (too-marginal) candidate.
_expectedOutcome: softLanded with a comfortable real-world margin (~1.0 m/s vs. the 2 m/s threshold, measured over 3 real runs). Angle stays 0 throughout since no Left/Right key is ever sent.
_note_2026_11_20: Last checkpoint moved from 21000 to 24000ms (test-timing margin only, not a physics constant) after the aligned-start investigation found the hand-built rebuild occasionally still airborne at t=21000 under the aligned click sequence's slightly different real-world timing (not yet landed by a few hundred ms to ~1s, not a behavior change) - giving comfortable margin for BOTH sides to have genuinely landed by the final checkpoint, rather than an artifact of which one happens to reach the checkpoint first. See docs/KIRO_NOTES.md, 'Third correction'.
